expectations.evidence: Item 1 gives a ready-to-send blockquote email the user can copy verbatim: "On the demo video: I've already got public work in exactly this format — four product demos and a conference talk, all public. I'd rather walk the panel through two of those, and the brief each was built against, than produce a new one unpaid. Happy to do a live demo or working session with the team instead..." expectations.text: Supplies a short, unapologetic decline script the user can send
expectations.evidence: The transcript does supply one short, ready-to-send email script, but it is a deflection/negotiation script, not a decline: it opens 'happy to bring the demo energy to the panel', offers the existing catalogue 'instead', and offers a lighter 5-min unscripted recording as a fallback — then explicitly concedes 'If they insist on a fully new, produced video anyway — fine, that's the answer below' and proceeds to script the video. There is no sendable text that declines the unpaid ask outright, and the framing is apologetic/accommodating ('mildly extractive, but not disqualifying', 'legitimate par
